## Learning Objectives

By the end of this week, you will be able to:

- Demonstrate knowledge of research methods concepts from Weeks 11-17 in a timed exam
- Finalise all project materials needed for data collection
- Practice running your group study from start to finish
- Complete and submit the Research Study Order Form

## MCQ Exam Information

### What to Expect

::: {.callout-note}
## Exam format
- **Number of questions**: 36 multiple-choice questions (5 investigations + 6 general)
- **Time allowed**: Check exam instructions
- **Topics**: All content from Weeks 11–17 (designs, IV/DV, hypotheses, test choice, p-values, correlation, operationalisation, replication, confounding, null hypothesis, population)
- **Format**: Paper-based exam
:::

### Exam Tips

::: {.callout-tip}
## Last-minute advice
1. **Read each question carefully** — look for key words like "NOT", "EXCEPT", "ALWAYS"
2. **Eliminate obviously wrong answers** — narrow down your choices
3. **Manage your time** — don't spend too long on any single question
4. **Answer every question** — no penalty for guessing
:::

## Project Toolkit — Phase 2 (Thursday Lab)

Phase 2 completes the toolkit so you are ready for **data collection in Week 19**.

Your group will:

1. **Recruitment Script** — Short script for approaching participants (template in toolkit)
2. **Data Recording Sheet** — Table for participant number, condition, DV score, scoring guide
3. **Stimulus materials** — Finalise word lists, images, questionnaires, etc. (toolkit has templates and examples)
4. **Researcher Procedure** — **Complete** the procedure you started in Week 17 (data recording, scoring, full script)
5. **Practice run** — Run the study on each other; fix any problems with timing, instructions, or materials
6. **Research Study Order Form** — List everything you need printed or provided for data collection day; submit by **end of this week**

::: {.callout-tip}
